name: Puerto Iguazú
summary: Use Puerto Iguazú for the Argentine trails and, with suitable border arrangements, Brazil’s panoramic side. Water levels and weather can close individual walkways.
seasonNote: Warm and humid much of the year; rainfall changes river flow and occasional walkway access.
arrival: IGR serves the Argentine side; IGU serves Brazil. Verify your airport and border requirements.
gettingAround: Local buses or arranged transfers reach the park; cross-border travel needs extra time.
cashTip: Carry pesos for local needs; Brazilian-side visits involve separate tickets and currency/card decisions.
foodTip: Try regional river fish, empanadas or chipá; ask about ingredients.
buyTip: Look for local craft with credible maker information; avoid wildlife products.
baseArea: Puerto Iguazú town for restaurants and bus connections.

connections.note: Border transfer and international formalities additional.

reviewSummary: The Argentine park listing has thousands of visitor reviews and a Travellers’ Choice badge. Plan independent days for Argentina and Brazil instead of assuming a single park ticket covers both.

items.name: Garganta del Diablo
items.summary: Boardwalks approach the falls’ most overwhelming cascade viewpoint.
items.expect: Spray, crowds and a train/walk sequence; water conditions may restrict access.
items.tip: Check the morning park bulletin and protect phones from spray.
items.priceNote: Included in Argentine national-park admission; buy one park ticket, not one ticket per trail.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The viewing approach puts visitors close to the falls’ great cascade.
Spray, sound and scale make this a sensory experience that photographs only partly convey.
visitFlow: Check the park bulletin for access and train arrangements.
Follow the open boardwalk to the viewing platform and protect electronics from spray.
items.tradeoffs: Spray, crowds and a train/walk sequence; water conditions may restrict access.

items.name: Upper & Lower circuits
items.summary: Complement the main cascade with varied viewpoints and forest walks.
items.expect: A full park day with heat, steps and long sections on foot.
items.tip: Bring water; do not feed coatis or other animals.
items.priceNote: Planning allowance for one foreign-adult park admission; peso tariff must be verified. Other park walks share this ticket.

review.note: Included in the researched destination shortlist; no verified numeric rating snapshot. Open current visitor reviews.

whyVisit: Different levels reveal the waterfall system from changing angles.
Forest links add wildlife habitat and quieter walking between the main viewpoints.
visitFlow: Choose open circuits according to mobility and heat.
Walk slowly with water breaks and never feed wildlife.
items.bestFor: A full day understanding the falls
items.tradeoffs: A full park day with heat, steps and long sections on foot.

items.name: Brazilian falls panorama
items.summary: The opposite bank offers a broad perspective on the waterfall system.
items.expect: A separate Brazilian park and an international border crossing.
items.tip: Check visa/entry rules and ticket inclusions; allow a full day including border buffers.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in ARS equivalent for transfer and Brazilian admission; payment is usually in BRL/card.

review.note: Foz do Iguaçu attraction listing for the falls; review count is not unique visitors and can include reports describing both countries.

whyVisit: The opposite bank offers a broad panorama of the waterfall system.
It complements the closer Argentine approaches with a different spatial overview.
visitFlow: Confirm border eligibility and Brazilian park tickets before departure.
Allow a full day with border buffers and follow the marked panoramic route.
items.tradeoffs: A separate Brazilian park and an international border crossing.

items.name: Three Frontiers landmark
items.summary: A river-confluence viewpoint where Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay meet.
items.expect: A compact town-side outing; evening shows have separate arrangements.
items.tip: Choose sunset with a planned return transfer if staying far away.
items.priceNote: Planning allowance for optional paid attractions; verify which national-side landmark you book.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The river confluence makes the meeting of three countries visible.
It offers a shorter town-side outing after a demanding park day.
visitFlow: Go at a suitable late-afternoon time.
View the confluence and keep a planned return transfer.
items.tradeoffs: A compact town-side outing; evening shows have separate arrangements.

items.name: Falls boat excursion
items.summary: An optional boat ride delivers a very wet close encounter with the river and falls.
items.expect: A paid adventure with age, health and weather restrictions.
items.tip: Read operator restrictions before booking; bring a change of clothes and waterproof storage.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate for a boat excursion; national park entry usually additional.

review.note: Included in the researched destination shortlist; no verified numeric rating snapshot. Open current visitor reviews.

whyVisit: The boat changes the falls from a distant view into a close river encounter.
It adds a distinct adventure for travellers who want more than boardwalk sightseeing.
visitFlow: Read operator restrictions and choose an authorised departure.
Protect belongings, wear the provided equipment and expect to get soaked.
items.tradeoffs: A paid adventure with age, health and weather restrictions.

items.name: Güirá Oga wildlife refuge
items.summary: Join an educator-led visit to a wildlife rehabilitation refuge.
items.expect: A guided rescue-centre visit, not a petting zoo or guaranteed wild sighting.
items.tip: General nonresident price in the retrieved operator page is ARS 35,000; confirm current rates.
items.area: RN12 · between town and the falls
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The visit explains rehabilitation and release work for regional wildlife.
An eco-trailer transfer and short guided trail give the encounter a clear structure.
visitFlow: Buy a place on the next available guided departure.
Follow the educator’s route and keep distance from animals.
items.tradeoffs: Groups and outdoor weather affect the pace; residents have different prices.

items.name: La Aripuca
items.summary: Explore a monumental timber structure and regional cultural park.
items.expect: A compact thematic attraction with shops and food.
items.tip: Operator requests direct contact for current prices; this range is a planning allowance.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The giant structure interprets the form of a traditional Guaraní trap.
Interpretive paths, craft displays and regional products add context to Misiones beyond waterfalls.
visitFlow: Walk around and inside the main timber structure where permitted.
Continue to the interpretive and craft areas.
items.tradeoffs: Commercial and interpretive elements are mixed; it is a smaller outing than the falls.

items.name: Sendero Macuco
items.summary: Take a forest trail to Salto Arrechea away from the main waterfall boardwalks.
items.expect: Operator lists7.6 km return, moderate difficulty and no services along the natural trail.
items.tip: Incremental trail cost assumed zero with valid park admission; do not add another full park entry for a same-day visit.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The route emphasises Misiones forest rather than the major cataracts.
A longer natural-surface walk provides a contrasting pace to the main circuits.
visitFlow: Ask rangers if the trail is open before starting.
Carry water and complete the out-and-back within the permitted hours.
items.tradeoffs: Weather-dependent closure and a real walking commitment; not an accessible boardwalk.

dayClusters.label: Arrive, eat and explore the town
dayClusters.note: Leave arrival time flexible, then visit town craft stalls and the river-confluence viewpoint near sunset. Arrange the return if accommodation is outside the centre.

dayClusters.label: A full Argentine falls day
dayClusters.note: Start at park opening and use the operating train/walkway plan. This is a full day; choose a shorter circuit if queues, heat or closures make all walks unrealistic. Both items share one Argentine park admission.

dayClusters.label: The Brazilian panorama
dayClusters.note: Keep a separate day for the international border, Brazilian park entry and return transfer. Check entry requirements for your passport and never assume the Argentine ticket covers this side.

dayClusters.label: Optional river adventure day
dayClusters.note: An additional day or a replacement for part of the Argentine trail day. Do not append it to every full-length walking circuit automatically; check age/health restrictions, weather, and any extra park admission.
